Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: MOSIP supports digital authentication via fingerprint biometrics and one-time passwords (OTPs). TECH5 ABIS enables 1:1 authentication for face, fingerprint, and iris. Authentication function present in the pilot but not fully deployed at national scale.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: OSIA-based identity system selected for ANIES explicitly includes financial inclusion and KYC. IDEMIA/SIA system designed for financial services access and payment services. ANIES planned cash transfer programme enabling financial and payment services access.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Comments: Civil registry corrections and late registrations require regularization via courts of first instance. Some judicial involvement in identity documentation. No formal structured judicial oversight mechanism for digital ID system found.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: EU/Belgium-funded civil registry modernization pilot active in 10 municipalities from 2023 (Enabel project). >105,000 records migrated to digital database. October 2023 law includes separate civil registry law. Linkage with digital ID system under development; not yet fully integrated at national scale.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Law No. L/2016/037/AN (2016) establishes data sharing and transfer rules, including prohibition on transfers to non-ECOWAS countries without equivalent protection. WURI Governance Framework signed 2023 establishes cross-border data sharing rules among member states. OSIA used for standardized data sharing.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: A specific law on identifying physical persons was passed by Guinea's National Transition Council in October 2023, casting some uncertainty on the existing legal framework per World Bank reports. The WURI programme also required a dedicated legal framework for foundational ID systems.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. L/2016/037/AN (enacted July 28, 2016) governs cybersecurity and personal data protection. Covers sensitive data, data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure), data controller obligations, and transfer rules. Provides for establishment of a national DPA (CNIL).

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Guinea's CNI (Carte Nationale d'Identite) is legally mandatory for citizens from age 15 (Decree D/95/254/PRG/SGG, 1995). Required at security checkpoints, borders, and for many official purposes. ANIES digital beneficiary card designed to provide legal identity.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Decree D/95/254/PRG/SGG (1995) provides legal framework for CNI. Law No. L/2016/037/AN on Cybersecurity and Personal Data Protection (2016). October 2023: National Transition Council passed a new law on identifying physical persons (separate from civil registry law). Multiple legal instruments in place.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: ANIES (National Agency for Economic and Social Inclusion) was the primary implementing agency for digital ID. WURI-Guinea was closed early in June 2024. New October 2023 law passed but institutional arrangements not fully consolidated. Maintenance responsibility unclear post-WURI closure.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Order A/2008/813/MEF/SGG (Ministry of Economy and Finance) sets stamp duty and fee rates for CNI issuance. FUGAS managed under Ministry of Labour. WURI funded by World Bank. No clear Ministry of Finance oversight of the digital ID system itself.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: TECH5's T5-ABIS supports face, fingerprint, and iris recognition for Guinea's national ID. Pilot evaluated all three biometric modalities. Existing CNI also required fingerprint. FUGAS biometric payroll system further confirms biometric capability.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Central database established since 1995 (CNI, Decree D/95/254 Art. 12 — 15-digit national identification number). MOSIP-based electronic database built for the WURI foundational ID pilot. FUGAS digital payroll database operational from 2024.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Guinea has a traditional national ID card (CNI) established since 1995, and launched a MOSIP/TECH5-based digital foundational ID via the WURI programme in 2021. A pilot issued 8,000 UNIs. The WURI-Guinea project was closed early in June 2024 before full national rollout. A new identification law was passed by the National Transition Council in October 2023. The FUGAS biometric payroll system launched in 2024/2025.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Guinea's ANIES adopted OSIA (Open Standards Identity APIs) standards for interoperability. Part of the WURI programme designed for regional ECOWAS interoperability and cross-border recognition. MOSIP platform supports interoperability. Strategy in design phase; full implementation not confirmed.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: ANIES/IDEMIA system designed to enable access to financial services via beneficiary card and cash transfer programme. OSIA system selected specifically to drive financial inclusion. No confirmed large-scale operational banking KYC use of digital ID reported.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: CNI has an official fee (15,000-25,000 GNF historically). Wikipedia notes 100,000/150,000 CFA. WURI/ANIES planned basic credentials at no cost to the population per WURI design principles. Mixed: traditional ID has fee; new digital ID targeted free issuance.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Guinea part of ECOWAS WURI programme for regional interoperability and mutual recognition of foundational ID credentials. WURI Governance Framework signed April 2023. ECOWAS ENBIC programme. Interoperability strategy validated in West Africa (Aug 2025). Guinea closed WURI early but regional framework exists.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: CNI mandatory from age 15 under Decree D/95/254/PRG/SGG (1995). WURI/ANIES system designed for 'all persons in the territory' without age restriction. MOSIP allows registration from young ages. Age 15 is the de facto lower bound for mandatory national ID.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The CNI is compulsory for all Guinean citizens from age 15 under Decree D/95/254/PRG/SGG (1995). Wikipedia lists it as 'Compulsory with a price of 100,000/150,000 CFA'. Required at security checkpoints and borders.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: Guinea's MOSIP system intended to enable healthcare access using digital ID. ANIES/WURI system described as providing access to healthcare, education, and social security services. No confirmed large-scale operational healthcare deployment found.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: WURI/MOSIP system explicitly designed for 'all persons in the territory—without consideration for nationality or legal status'. ANIES system targets inclusive coverage. MOSIP system includes non-citizens living in the country.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: ~40% of Guineans estimated to have a government ID (2020 MOSIP pilot data). Only ~20% had CNI in 2013 (CRC4D). WURI target was 80% coverage by 2024, but only 8,000 persons received a UNI through the pilot (closed June 2024). Coverage remains low.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: Guinea's MOSIP pilot included validation of technology and evaluation of biometric devices from three providers (interoperability testing). WURI includes data security measures (authentication, role-based access, VPN encryption). FUGAS system includes biometric verification. No evidence of formal independent external security audit.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: M2M Group deployed a biometric identification system for social safety nets project in Guinea in 2018 (World Bank funded), capable of enrolling several million people. WURI/ANIES digital ID designed to link vulnerable populations to government support programs. Social safety net use confirmed.
